overview: This Senate resolution supports naming February 2026 "Career and Technical Education Month." Career and technical education, often called CTE, is schooling that teaches job skills for specific trades and careers, offered in high schools, technical centers and two-year colleges. The resolution recognizes CTE's role in preparing a skilled workforce and encourages teachers, school counselors, administrators and parents to promote it as a respected path for students. It notes the anniversary of a 1917 law that was the first major federal investment in this kind of education. The Senate approved it on February 26, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution highlights an education path that leads many students to well-paying, in-demand jobs and encourages schools and families to treat it with the same respect as a four-year degree.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide any funding for career and technical programs.
